{{nihongo|'''Ichinomiya Sengen Shrine'''|一宮浅間神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Kai Province]].

'''Ichinomiya Sengen Shrine'' (Ichinomiya Sengenjinja <ref>Some call it a kana (Japanese historical place name system, etc.) which is pronounced as 'Ichinomiya Asamajinja'.</ref>) is {{ill|Yamanashi Prefecture|Q132720|qid=Q132720}}{{ill|Nishiyatsushiro District, Yamanashi|Q1131467|qid=Q1131467}}{{ill|Ichikawamisato|Q1204453|qid=Q1204453}}{{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} located in Takada. {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} ({{ill|Myōjin Taisha|Q9610964|qid=Q9610964}}) {{ill|Shikinai Ronsha|Q135022904|qid=Q135022904}}, {{ill|Q712534|lt=Old shrine rank}} is {{ill|Son-sha|ja|村社|qid=Q134917284}}.

The enshrinement site is located south of Takada village, at the northwestern tip of the Nishiyashiro Plateau, and in ancient times the shrine was simply called ``Ichinomiya'', ``Ichinomiya Myojin'', and ``Ichikawa Ichinomiya''.

=== Setsusha ===
When the {{ill|Ansei great earthquakes|Q849463|qid=Q849463|lt=Great Earthquakes}} struck the area in {{ill|1854|Q7670|qid=Q7670}} ({{ill|Ansei|Q1327259|qid=Q1327259}} first year), he made efforts to help the victims. There is also a branch shrine that originated from the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ikushō}} where {{ill|Daikan|Q10263740|qid=Q10263740}} {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=kendo Arai}} and {{ill|myōshu|Q110095935|qid=Q110095935}} Yasukiyo Yoda were enshrined during their lifetimes, as well as five other shrines.

According to the "Shaki," the old shrines were Misaki Daimyojin in Shimo-Otorii Village (currently {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Misaki Shrine}} in Shimo-Otorii, Ichikawa Misato Town), Sutaka Daimyojin in Kurosawa Village (currently {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Sutaka Shrine}} in Kurosawa, Ichikawa Town), and Sanno Gongen (currently {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Hiei Shrine}} in Kurosawa, Ichikawa Village). (Ichikawa Misato Town)||Hiei Shrine}}) and other nearby shrines were named {{ill|Sessha|Q135009904|qid=Q135009904}}<ref name="Heibonsha place name"/>.

=== Festival ===
* {{ill|Reisai|Q11385469|qid=Q11385469}} ({{ill|November 3|Q2995|qid=Q2995}})
: According to the "Shaki", it used to be that November's Dragon's Day was a national holiday, and on that day, a mikoshi (portable shrine) was carried from Mt. Gosatai. Also, during the Takeda clan era, a rice festival was held on April tatsuhi, and after that, Wakamiya Hachiman Shrine in Oi (now {{ill|Minami-Alps, Yamanashi|Q824000|qid=Q824000}} Tokaichi Market, about 6 {{ill|Kilometre|Q828224|qid=Q828224}} north of {{ill|Koma District|Q11479803|qid=Q11479803}} It is said that a mikoshi was passed to (Minami Alps City) Wakamiya Hachiman Shrine (Minami Alps City), where feudal lords joined in the procession, and cavalry warriors also assembled their horses, and the area came to be known as ``Twenty Horse Fields.'' It is also said that a market was built on the land where the mikoshi was parked, and that is where the name of the current Minami Alps City Old Market came from. In addition, there was a ritual for the first harvest on September 19th that began in {{ill|1635|Q6879|qid=Q6879}} (Kanei 12th year), but most of these rituals have ceased to exist.

It has been reported by Takashi Okazaki that statues of the four gods and four beasts are arranged alternately in the inner ward of the mirror back, and on the outer ward, the inscription ``'''May 5th day of the 1st year of Akagarasu, Zosukaku Meisho, Hyakko Kiyodo, Prince of Clothes, Descendants of Nobu, 10,000 years of life''' has been cast. This divine beast mirror was reported to the academic society by {{ill|Shūichi Gotō|Q11488456|qid=Q11488456}} in {{ill|1924|Q2173|qid=Q2173}} ({{ill|Taishō era|Q329174|qid=Q329174}}13).:"{{ill|Chiwu|Q8011978|qid=Q8011978}}" written in the inscription is {{jalink|Wu of {{ill|Three Kingdoms|Q185043|qid=Q185043|lt=Three Kingdoms Period}} (Mikuni)|Q274488|Wu}}'s {{ill|Era name|Q256408|qid=Q256408}}, which corresponds to {{ill|238|Q30058|qid=Q30058|lt=238 AD}}, It is valuable as the oldest of Japan's era-inscribed mirrors, and as a relic that suggests the possibility of negotiations between Japan ({{ill|Wa (name of Japan)|Q1378053|qid=Q1378053}}) and Wu at the time. In 1933 (Showa 8), it was recognized as {{ill|Important Art Object|Q11644862|qid=Q11644862}}, and in 1979, it was again designated as an Important Cultural Property. (1976) Ministry of Education Notification No. 112, June 6, [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/9991 Agency for Cultural Affairs, “Nationally Designated Cultural Properties Database”] (accessed March 23, 2010). </ref>.

=== Yamanashi Prefecture designated cultural property ===
*1 bronze mirror (tangible cultural property (craft), {{ill|1968|Q2644|qid=Q2644}} (February 8, 1968))
:A {{ill|Bōseikyō|Q130529515|qid=Q130529515|lt=manufactured}} {{ill|Bronze mirror|ca|Espill de bronze|es|Espejo de bronce|fr|Miroir en bronze|ja|銅鏡|ko|동경 (거울)|my|ကြေးမုံ|no|Bronsespeil|simple|Bronze mirror|uk|Бронзове дзеркало|zh|铜镜|qid=Q1041984|lt=bronze mirror}} that was excavated along with the above divine beast mirror. The flat border of the plain text has a double comb-tooth pattern that divides it into inner and outer wards. </ref>.

=== Others ===
*{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Zuijin}} 2 statues
:{{ill|Attack|qid=Attack|lt=Attack}}{{ill|Sokutai|Q1156828|qid=Q1156828|lt=Sokutai figure}}. On the back of the {{ill|Ungyō|Q137190286|qid=Q137190286}} statue, there is an inscription written in ink by {{ill|1557|Q6595|qid=Q6595}} ({{ill|Kōji (Muromachi period)|Q1143910|qid=Q1143910|lt=Koji}}), making it a valuable piece of medieval work inscribed in Yamanashi Prefecture, which is relatively rare.
*Ichinomiya Sengen Miyacho
:Edo period {{ill|Chronicle|Q185363|qid=Q185363}}. Paper and ink calligraphy. Dimensions are 24.8 cm long and 16.9 cm wide. Total of 7 books. The seventh book states that the shogunate was responsible for the {{ill|Flood|Q8068|qid=Q8068}} that occurred in Kai in {{ill|Enkyō (Edo period)|Q1183728|qid=Q1183728}}4 ({{ill|1747|Q7596|qid=Q7596}}). jalink|Tottori Domain|Q905521}} and {{ill|Oka Domain|Q8192275|qid=Q8192275}} are known to be ordered to carry out restoration work.
